title: Information Intermediaries in Monopolistic Screening
abstract: arXiv:2604.09343v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We investigate the relationship between product offerings, information dissemination, and consumer decision-making in a monopolistic screening environment in which consumers lack information about their valuation of quality-differentiated products. An intermediary, who is driven by the objective of maximizing consumer surplus but is also biased towards high-quality products, provides recommendations after the monopolist announces the menu of product choices. We characterize the monopolist's profit-maximizing finite-item menu. Our results show that as intermediaries place greater emphasis on consumer surplus over product quality, sellers are prompted to strategically expand their product range. Intriguingly, this augmented product variety decreases economic efficiency compared to scenarios where direct seller-to-consumer information provision is the norm. translated_title: 垄断筛选环境中的信息中介
translated_abstract: 我们研究了在垄断筛选环境中产品供应、信息传播与消费者决策之间的关系，在该环境中，消费者缺乏关于自己对质量差异化产品估值的信息。一个以最大化消费者剩余为目标、但同时也偏向高质量产品的中介，会在垄断者公布产品选择菜单之后提供推荐。我们刻画了垄断者实现利润最大化的有限项目菜单。研究结果表明，当中介越加重视消费者剩余而非产品质量时，卖方会被促使战略性地扩大其产品范围。有趣的是，与卖方直接向消费者提供信息为常态的情形相比，这种产品种类的增加反而降低了经济效率。信息中介在塑造消费者福利方面的作用被证明是至关重要的。
tldr: 本研究刻画了垄断筛选环境下中介推荐机制中的最优产品菜单，发现中介越重视消费者剩余越会促使卖方扩大产品种类，但这种扩张反而降低了经济效率，凸显了信息中介在塑造消费者福利中的关键作用。
en_tdlr: In a monopolistic screening environment, information intermediaries that emphasize consumer surplus induce sellers to strategically expand product variety, which paradoxically reduces economic efficiency, highlighting the pivotal role of intermediaries in shaping consumer welfare.
